newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav Bor 8-mo copper ore output 9 mln T - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav Bor 8-mo copper ore output 9 mln T - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest mining and smelting complex, Rudarsko Topionicarski Basen Bor (RTB Bor), produced nearly nine million tonnes of copper ore from January to August, the Belgrade daily Borba reported on Tuesday.
RTB Bor produced 33,700 tonnes of copper concentrate and 65,000 tonnes of cathode copper in the same period, Borba quoted the latest company figures as saying.
RTB Bor officials said the company did not wish to comment on the report.
In the same eight-month period, RTB Bor exported $40 million worth of copper products from its own locally-mined raw materials to Greece, Italy, Hungary, Bulgaria and Ukraine.

In June, RTB Bor said it had targeted 1996 output of cathode copper at 125,000 tonnes, including around 74,000 tonnes from its own raw materials. It planned to export around 60 percent of its annual production.
The complex's total refining capacities are 170,000 tonnes of cathode copper.
The current price of copper on the international metals exchange of around around $2,000 per tonne is not enough for RTB Bor to operate at a profit, the Borba report quoted the company as saying.

"If this (price) trend continues in the following months, RTB Bor will suffer substantial losses. In such circumstances it would be difficult to achieve the planned $200 million worth of exports," the report said.
